subject.name: NodeRoom note-shaped surfaces, after the note-surface fix — NoteworthyInbox item list and NotebookDigestWorkbench block list
subject.surface: The same two entry lists as the baseline receipt (score-noderoom-note-surfaces-stream-not-chrome-before), re-scored after the feat/note-surface-dna change: inbox items and digest blocks now render as divider-separated stream rows instead of filled cards.
subject.evidenceRef: source, noderoom branch feat/note-surface-dna: src/app/styles.css (.r-inbox-item + .r-inbox-item divider, no per-item background), src/ui/workArtifacts/work-artifacts.css (.wa-notebook-block + .wa-notebook-block divider, zero-width base border, gap 0)

appliesWhenSatisfied: review-in-time-order is the primary job: unchanged from the baseline receipt
entries are short and heterogeneous: unchanged
organization is emergent rather than upfront: unchanged

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: long-form documents with internal heading hierarchy (obs-fabric-contrast/f1)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Unchanged: neither surface renders headed long-form documents.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: workflows where retrieval at 10k+ items dominates capture (obs-evernote-contrast/f1)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Unchanged: both lists remain bounded (48 digest blocks, inbox digest grouping at 5+).

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: multi-user triage queues where list-vs-detail is load-bearing
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Unchanged: no list-vs-detail pane pair exists on either surface.

anchors.0: multi-pane chrome with bordered note cards, in the shape of Evernote's three simultaneous panes (obs-evernote-contrast/f1, f2)
anchors.1: one scrolling column, but every entry is a bordered or filled card with its own background and corner radius
anchors.2: mixed treatment: some entries de-carded or the column unified, card chrome remains elsewhere in the entry list
anchors.3: entries separated by dividers only, no per-entry card chrome; residual simultaneous-pane structure remains outside the entry list
anchors.4: a single divider-separated column and nothing else — no cards, no per-note background, no simultaneous second pane (obs-mew-stream/f1)

criteria.question: How are NoteworthyInbox entries bounded — divider or card?

citations.note: Entries now meet at a 1px rule (.r-inbox-item + .r-inbox-item { border-top: 1px solid var(--line) }) with no per-entry background, radius, or margin. Failed items keep a danger tint plus an inset left edge — failure-state signaling on a trust surface, deliberately retained — and researching items keep an inset accent edge as a live indicator.
The bordered-card-per-note counterexample shape no longer describes this list.

criteria.finding: Divider-separated stream rows. State styling survives on exactly the rows that carry state, which is the difference between chrome and signal.

criteria.question: How are NotebookDigestWorkbench blocks bounded — divider or card?

citations.note: Blocks lost their border, radius, and background; siblings meet at a 1px rule with zero grid gap. The base border is declared at zero width solid so the full-screen [data-detail=notebook] variant's border-width override keeps its own divider — the treatment that variant already used, now shared by the default view. needs_review keeps its tint and gains an inset accent edge: pending-review state, not chrome.
No bordered tiles remain in the entry column.

criteria.finding: Divider-separated stream entries, consistent between the digest's default and full-screen views.

criteria.question: Does either surface split into simultaneous panes before the entries can be read?

citations.note: Unchanged from baseline: the digest keeps its blocks + 28% aside grid. The aside hosts patch previews with before/after diffs — proposal and diff trust surfaces governed by the trust-surfaces contract — and folding it away was explicitly out of this change's licence.
Mew's one-column absolute remains unmet by the digest. Recorded unimproved, on purpose.

criteria.finding: Unimproved and honestly so: the aside is review tooling for pending proposals, and removing it to satisfy a note-surface rule would trade a trust surface for a style point.

scoreBasis: Ladder: the subject sits at the highest anchor it fully satisfies. c1 and c2 now satisfy the divider-only entry treatment; c3's residual aside holds the subject at anchor 3 rather than 4.
notScored: The full notebook editor (Tiptap document surface) — outside this rule per its doesNotApplyWhen, unchanged.
The wall artifact's capture cards — spatial canvas entries, not a time-ordered stream, unchanged.

Runtime render: this after-receipt, like the baseline, scores from source; the repo's unit suite and the trust-surface selftest were run, but no computed-style audit of these two selectors was performed.
Whether readers perceive the divider treatment as easier to scan — audience-task evidence (M3) does not exist for this rule yet, per the rule's own tier ladder.
boundary: Scored from source on branch feat/note-surface-dna, diffed against commit 9c99889f. The claims about which selectors changed are verifiable in the branch diff; the claim that no other selector re-cards these entries was checked by grep over both stylesheets and the [data-detail=notebook] variant block.
